title: Release cargo runner and LTS gatekeeper for private deployments
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Build 'Release Cargo Runner' (RCR) and an accompanying 'LTS Gatekeeper' service to handle coordinated artifact delivery, staged rollouts, and compatibility checks for Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) upgrades. Rationale: current private upgrade flow is ad-hoc across teams and relies on several one-off scripts. We need a repeatable, auditable, and policy-driven runner that performs artifact distribution, preflight checks, transactional migration handoffs, cohorted canaries, and automated fallback. The LTS Gatekeeper provides channel-aware blocking rules (stable/LTS vs latest), enforces pinned-version policies per-customer, and gates rollouts based on telemetry and compatibility signals.

Scope and deliverables:
- Release Cargo Runner (service + lightweight CLI): orchestrates staged artifact deployment to private clusters, runs pre/post hooks, executes transactional DB migration wrappers, and emits structured events to Console telemetry.
- LTS Gatekeeper (policy engine): evaluates customer-level channel policies, enforces rollout gates (SLO/compat thresholds), and exposes an API for Console and Private control plane to query allowed upgrade windows.
- Orchestrated migration primitives: idempotent migration runner, migration-state snapshotting, preflight dry-run mode, and rollback orchestration.
- Observability & Audit: per-release audit trail, tokenized operation tracing, release-level metrics (success_rate, rollback_rate, median_time_to_restore), and Confluence runbook link.
- Safety features: staged cohorts, automatic halt on threshold breach, emergency rollback path, and manual approval hook for high-impact customers.

Design notes and decisions:
- Naming: we intentionally avoid 'orchestrator' in API surface to reduce collision with existing k8s operator names; 'Cargo Runner' is the delivery primitive and is implementable as a stateful controller + CLI.
- Migration strategy: adopt a two-phase commit style for DB-related migrations where a migration manifest declares forward/reverse steps and validation probes. For clusters without DB access we will fall back to schema-less compatibility checks.
- Rollout policy model: allow declarative policies per-customer (JSON/YAML) with fields: channel (lts/stable/latest), max_cohort_size, success_threshold_pct, probe_window_seconds, and telemetry_hooks.
- Fallback model: define automatic fallback to previous pinned LTS image if Gatekeeper detects sustained regression > configurable threshold for N minutes.

Integration points (non-exhaustive):
- Console: rollout UI, approval buttons, and progress stream.
- Private control plane agent: asset fetch, checksum verification, and local execution of migration jobs.
- KMS: encrypted artifact signatures for air-gapped installs.
- Audit logging: forward events to customer-managed syslog or our Audit API depending on deployment mode.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
acceptance_criteria: RCR can deliver artifacts to a private cluster and record an auditable release event.
Gatekeeper can evaluate a per-customer policy and return allow/deny for a candidate version.
A staged canary rollout can be executed with cohorts and automatic halt when success_rate < configured threshold.
Transactional migration manifest supports dry-run and rollback and has an idempotent execution path.
Console shows per-release telemetry (token-level cost delta, error rate, latency regression) and links to runbook/PRs.
comments: 2026-03-02 — Architecture sync: aligned on two-component approach (cargo runner + gatekeeper). Agreed RCR will use a small state machine persisted to our DB to track phases (prepare, deliver, migrate, verify, finalize). — Diego

2026-03-05 — Design review: PM asked for explicit customer opt-out for automatic rollbacks. Added opt-out flag and manual approval gate for enterprise customers. Action: add UI toggle and API flag. — Asha

2026-03-07 — Engineering spike: built PoC CLI that uploads release artifacts to a private artifact mirror and triggers a remote agent via webhook. Found edge case where private clusters block outbound webhooks; we will support pull-based agent polling. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rcr/pull/34 — Diego

2026-03-09 — Security review kickoff: noted requirement for KMS-signed artifacts for air-gapped customers and HSM integration for key rotation. Security recommended threat model doc and signed attestation for migration steps. Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RINF/Release+Cargo+Runner+Design — Priya (Security)

2026-03-11 — Observability plan: define metrics and tracing keys. Proposed metrics: rcr.release.duration_seconds, rcr.release.rollback_rate, gatekeeper.policy.evaluations, gatekeeper.blocked_requests. Suggested linking to Console per-release breakdown. — Observability team

2026-03-12 — Blocker identified: existing private agent cannot run migration manifests that require elevated DB roles. Next: design a temporary credential broker flow and expiring short-lived DB tokens. — Diego
work_items: Implement RCR state machine and persistent run record.
Gatekeeper policy evaluation API and UI hooks in Console.
Migration manifest schema and dry-run validation tool.
Agent changes: pull model and execution sandbox for migration steps.
Telemetry: per-release metric set and alerting rules.
notes: Links: design doc (Confluence) https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RINF/Release+Cargo+Runner+Design; runbook draft https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RINF/RCR+Runbook; initial PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/rcr/pull/34. Risk: high operational complexity for customers with strict change windows; mitigation: conservative default cohort sizes and explicit on-call playbook. Next steps: finalize migration manifest spec, implement Gatekeeper proto, and deliver PoC to 2 pilot customers by 2026-04-01.
